summary_hint: E-SIGN consent by {consumer name}, affirmatively consented {consent_date_time}, delivery {delivery_method}, version {consent_version}.

typed_core.name: consumer_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose consent (flattened from person[]; primary signer)

typed_core.name: consumer_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second consumer on joint consent

typed_core.name: consumer_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — how many consumers the raw name string held

typed_core.name: affirmative_consent_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — the headline: did the consumer affirmatively consent

typed_core.name: consent_version
typed_core.why: disambiguator/identity — which version of the consent was signed

typed_core.name: consent_scope_and_duration
typed_core.why: processor — how long / what the consent covers

typed_core.name: records_covered
typed_core.why: processor — which records the consent applies to (flattened from string[])

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — links consent to the loan file

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: identity — document date when no explicit consent timestamp

rejected.name: hardware_software_requirements, right_to_paper_copies, paper_copy_fees, consent_withdrawal_procedure, contact_update_procedure, consequences_of_withdrawal, hardware_requirement_change_notice, ability_to_access_or_demonstration
rejected.reason: boilerplate disclosure text; no field-level consumer -> catch-all

rejected.name: ip_address_or_device_metadata
rejected.reason: restricted audit metadata; no consumer; must not sit unmasked

encoding_variations: Consent timestamp appears as an audit datetime, a signature date, or prose ('I consent on this day...'). No datetime coercer -> str; keep document_issue_date (date) as a fallback.
'Affirmative consent' may be a checkbox, an 'I Agree' button capture, or a typed-name signature — all mean the same yes; keep the raw indicator plus electronic_signature.

open_questions.q: Is any compliance-completeness rule planned? If a future rule checks that all ESIGN required disclosures are present, several rejected boilerplate fields (right_to_paper_copies, hardware_software_requirements, consent_withdrawal_procedure) become the floor.
options: leave in catch-all until rule exists
open_questions.recommendation: leave in catch-all until that rule exists; promote then

open_questions.q: consent_date_time vs document_issue_date. Both may be present; datetime has no coercer.
options: keep datetime as str plus document_issue_date fallback
open_questions.recommendation: keep the datetime as str for the exact timestamp and document_issue_date (date) as a coercible fallback

open_questions.q: Joint consent modeling. Two consumers with two emails/phones — flat pairing may misalign which email belongs to which name.
options: keep raw lists as str and flag alignment as a known limitation
open_questions.recommendation: keep raw lists as str and flag alignment as a known limitation rather than nesting GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): keep the raw email/phone lists flat as str; flag the alignment as a known limitation (no nesting).

notes: No rules today, so no rule floor. This is an ESIGN Act consent disclosure. Most of its CORE catalog fields are boilerplate disclosure text (hardware requirements, right-to-paper-copy language, withdrawal procedure) — a processor does not read those field-by-field; they belong in the catch-all. The load-bearing facts are who consented, when, whether affirmatively, and which version.

consumer_email_addresses needs registration, pre_masked false (raw email; the snapshot must mask). consumer_phone_numbers needs registration, pre_masked false (raw phone). Neither is in the 7-field registry.
ip_address_or_device_metadata (catalog OPTIONAL, restricted) is rejected from typed core, but noted: if ever captured it must NOT land in the unmasked catch-all. Flag.

Prompt hint (doc-level): tell the model this is an ESIGN Act consent; the legally required elements (right to paper, hardware/software requirements, withdrawal right) are present as disclosure text — capture them into additional_sections, not typed core.
Prompt hint (doc-level): email and phone here are consumer PII — extract verbatim, do not normalize or mask (the snapshot masks raw PII).
